Load required packages:
```{r, message=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(misty)
library(rstatix)
library(knitr)
library(Rmisc)
library(xtable)
```

Import processed data.
```{r}
dat <- read.csv2('Data/Study2_data_processed.csv')
```

# Sample descriptives

*Note that the following demographic variables were removed from the data sets, to guarantee anonymity: Gender, age, citizenship, job status, educational background.*

```{r, echo=FALSE}
dat %>%
  summarise(mean = mean(BMI, na.rm = TRUE),
            sd = sd(BMI, na.rm = TRUE),
            min = min(BMI, na.rm = TRUE),
            max = max(BMI, na.rm = TRUE)
            ) %>%
  kable(format = 'markdown', digits = 2, 
        col.names = c('Mean BMI', 'Std. Dev.(BMI)', 'Min.(BMI)', 'Max.(BMI)'),
        caption = 'Body mass index')

```

# Control analyses

In these analyses, we checked whether the results of the main analyses remained stable when controlling for the belief in a causal health-taste relationship and the general health interest (GHI).

Also, participants saw the food ratings from two contexts, "Cafeterias" and "Restaurants". We randomised which of the names was for the 1st and 2nd context, respectively. The variable `random_context` indicates how the contexts were named. Further, we randomised the background colours on which the 1st and 2nd context were presented (light pink and light green). The variable `random_colour` indicates which context had which colour. 

To check whether these individual characteristics and randomisations affected the results, we ran the main analyses again (for details, see R markdown file `Study2_analyses.Rmd`), while including the (un)healthy-tasty belief and GHI as covariates and randomisations of context names and colours as factors.


```{r, include=FALSE}
# Turn the id and group variables into factors and add labels to the groups.
dat <-
  dat %>% 
  mutate(id = factor(id),
         condition = factor(condition, 
                            levels = c('1', '2', '3'), 
                            labels = c('Harmonious', 'Conflicting', 'Control')),
         random_colour = factor(random_colour,
                                 levels = c('1', '2'),
                                 labels = c('1st context pink, 2nd context green', '1st context green, 2nd context pink')),
         random_context = factor(random_context,
                                 levels = c('1', '2'),
                                 labels = c('1st context "Cafeterias", 2nd context "Restaurants"', '1st context "Restaurants", 2nd context "Cafeterias"'))
  )
```

## Descriptive statistics of covariates

```{r, echo=FALSE}
dat %>%
  summarise(mean = mean(causal_HT, na.rm = TRUE),
            sd = sd(causal_HT, na.rm = TRUE),
            min = min(causal_HT, na.rm = TRUE),
            max = max(causal_HT, na.rm = TRUE)
            ) %>%
  kable(format = 'markdown', digits = 2, 
        col.names = c('Mean belief', 'Std. Dev.(belief)', 'Min.(belief)', 'Max.(belief)'),
        caption = 'Belief in a causal health-taste relationship')

```


```{r, echo=FALSE}
dat %>%
  summarise(mean = mean(GHI, na.rm = TRUE),
            sd = sd(GHI, na.rm = TRUE),
            min = min(GHI, na.rm = TRUE),
            max = max(GHI, na.rm = TRUE)
            ) %>%
  kable(format = 'markdown', digits = 2, 
        col.names = c('Mean GHI', 'Std. Dev.(GHI)', 'Min.(GHI)', 'Max.(GHI)'),
        caption = 'General health interest')

```

## Perceived health-taste relationship within contexts

```{r, include=FALSE}
# Restructure data into long format for the mixed ANOVA, convert the context variable into a factor.
dat_long <-
  dat %>% 
  select(id, condition, ht_rel_c1, ht_rel_c2, causal_HT, GHI, random_colour, random_context) %>% 
  pivot_longer(cols = c('ht_rel_c1', 'ht_rel_c2'), 
                       names_to = 'context',
                       values_to = 'ht_rel') %>% 
  mutate(context = rec(context, '"ht_rel_c1" = 1; "ht_rel_c2" = 2')) %>%
  mutate(context =factor(context,
                         levels = c('1', '2'),
                         labels= c('1st Context', '2nd Context')))
```

### ANCOVA
```{r}
acv_ht_rel <-
  anova_test(
  data = dat_long, dv = ht_rel, wid = id,
  between = c(condition, random_context, random_colour), covariate = c(causal_HT, GHI), within = context, type = 3, effect.size = 'pes')
```

```{r, echo=FALSE}
options(dplyr.summarise.inform = FALSE) # Deactivate the warning message
colnames(acv_ht_rel) <- c('Effect','df/nominator', 'df/denominator', '$F$', '$p$', 'Sig.', 'partial $\\eta^2$')
rownames(acv_ht_rel) <- c('Causal HT belief', 'General health interest', 'Base rate manipulation','Context randomisation', 'Colour randomisation', 'Context', 'Base rate manipulation*Context randomisation','Base rate manipulation*Colour randomisation', 'Context randomisation*Colour randomisation','Causal HT belief*Context', 'General health interest*Context', 'Base rate manipulation*Context', 'Name randomisation*Context', 'Colour randomisation*Context', 'Base rate manipulation\\*Context randomisation*Colour randomisation', 'Base rate manipulation\\*Context randomisation*Context', 'Base rate manipulation\\*Colour randomisation*Context', 'Context randomisation\\*Colour randomisation*Context', 'Base rate manipulation\\*Context randomisation\\*Colour randomisation*Context')

kable(acv_ht_rel[,-1],format = 'markdown',  digits = 2,
      caption = 'Results of the ANCOVA testing the effect of base rate manipulation and context on the perceived health-taste relationship')
```
Most importantly, the main effect of base rate manipulation remained stable. There was a large effect of the belief in a causal health-taste relationship on the perceived health-taste relationship.

There was an unexpected small interaction effect between base rate manipulation and colour randomisation. To follow up, we calculated pairwise comparisons of the health-taste relationship between base rate manipulations within each colour randomisation group.

#### Follow-up: Pairwise comparisons

```{r, echo=FALSE}
ht_rel_pw <- 
  dat_long %>%
  group_by(random_colour) %>% 
  pairwise_t_test(ht_rel ~ condition, p.adjust.method = "bonferroni")

kable(ht_rel_pw[,-c(2, 5:6)], format = 'markdown', digits = 2,
        caption = 'Pairwise comparisons of the perceived health-taste relationship between base rate manipulations within colour randomisation groups',
        col.names = c('Colour randomisation', 'Base rate manipulation 1', 'Base rate manipulation 2', '$p$', 'Sign', '$p.adj$', 'Sign. adj.'))
```

#### Descriptive statistics

```{r, echo=FALSE}
# Check the mean, standard deviation, standard error and 95% confidence interval of the perceived health-taste relationship in each base rate manipulation and colour randomisation group.
ht_rel_sum <- summarySE(dat_long, measurevar='ht_rel', groupvars=c('random_colour', 'condition'))
ht_rel_sum %>% 
  kable(format = 'markdown', digits = 2,
        col.names = c('Colour randomisation', 'Condition', 'N', 'Mean relationship', 'Std. Dev.', 'Std. Error', '95% CI'), 
        caption = 'Mean perceived health-taste relationship by base rate manipulation and colour randomisation')

```

According to pairwise comparisons, the perceived health-taste relationship did not differ between the harmonious and control base rate manipulation, when the first context had a pink and the second context had a green background colour. Otherwise, there were differences between all base rate manipulations in both groups.

## Perceived health-taste relationship across contexts

### ANCOVA

```{r, message=FALSE}
acv_ht_rel_ov <-
  anova_test(
    data = dat, dv = belief_ht_overall_R,
    between = c(condition, random_context, random_colour), covariate = c(causal_HT, GHI), type = 3,
    effect.size = 'pes')

```

```{r, echo=FALSE}

colnames(acv_ht_rel_ov) <- c('Effect','df/nominator', 'df/denominator', '$F$', '$p$', 'Sig.', 'partial $\\eta^2$')
rownames(acv_ht_rel_ov) <- c('Causal HT belief', 'General health interest', 'Base rate manipulation', 'Context randomisation', 'Colour randomisation',  'Base rate manipulation*Context randomisation', 'Base rate manipulation*Colour randomisation', 'Context randomisation*Colour randomisation', 'Base rate manipulation\\*Context randomisation*Colour randomisation')

kable(acv_ht_rel_ov[,-1], format = 'markdown',  digits = 2,
      caption = 'Results of the ANCOVA testing the effect of base rate manipulation on the perceived health-taste relationship across contexts')
```
Most importantly, the main effect of base rate manipulation on the perceived health-taste relationship across contexts remained stable. There was a medium-sized effect of the belief in a causal health-taste relationship on the perceived health-taste relationship. 

There was an unexpected medium-sized interaction between base rate manipulation and colour randomisation. To follow up, we calculated pairwise comparisons of the health-taste relationship between base rate manipulations within each colour randomisation group.

#### Follow-up: Pairwise comparisons

```{r, echo=FALSE}
ht_rel_ov_pw <- 
  dat %>%
  group_by(random_colour) %>% 
  pairwise_t_test(belief_ht_overall_R ~ condition, p.adjust.method = "bonferroni")

kable(ht_rel_pw[,-c(2, 5:6)], format = 'markdown', digits = 2,
        caption = 'Pairwise comparisons of the perceived health-taste relationship between base rate manipulations within randomisation groups',
        col.names = c('Colour randomisation', 'Base rate manipulation 1', 'Base rate manipulation 2', '$p$', 'Sign', '$p.adj$', 'Sign. adj.'))
```

#### Descriptive statistics

```{r, echo=FALSE}
# Check the mean, standard deviation, standard error and 95% confidence interval of the contingency belief in each base rate manipulation and colour randomisation group.
ht_rel_ov_sum <- summarySE(dat, measurevar='belief_ht_overall_R', groupvars=c('random_colour', 'condition'))
ht_rel_ov_sum %>% 
  kable(format = 'markdown', digits = 2,
        col.names = c('Colour randomisation', 'Base rate manipulation', 'N', 'Mean belief', 'Std. Dev.', 'Std. Error', '95% CI'), 
        caption = 'Mean perceived health-taste relationship by base rate manipulation and colour randomisation')

```

According to pairwise comparisons, the perceived health-taste relationship did not differ between the harmonious and control base rate manipulation, when the first context had a pink and the second context had a green background colour. Otherwise, there were differences between all base rate manipulations in both groups.

## Correlations between causal health-taste relationship and dependent variables

There were medium-sized effects of the belief in a causal health-taste relationship on the perceived health-taste relationship. To follow up, we calculated Pearson correlations between the causal health-taste belief and the perceived health-taste relationship.

```{r, echo=FALSE}
dat_cor <- 
  dat %>% 
  select(causal_HT,
         starts_with('ht_rel'),
         belief_ht_overall_R)

cor<-round(cor(dat_cor),2)
upper<-cor
upper[upper.tri(cor)]<-""
upper<-as.data.frame(upper)
upper
```

## Summary

The results remained stable when controlling for general health interest, belief in a causal health-taste relationship and the randomisation of context names and background colours. 

There were some unexpected influences of the context background colours on the differences between the control and harmonious base rate manipulation, but this did not change the main findings.

General health interest did not affect the outcome variables in any way. The larger participants' general belief that a food made healthier is also tastier and vice versa, the more did they perceive a healthy-tasty relationship within each context as well as across contexts.
